## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

Part **13/n** of the Kimi K3 / Dist-MoE training stack. Stacked on
[#5685](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5685). A separate 14/n
provides the full-scale MXFP8 recipe consumers.

## Why

The existing remat policy applies each save-region pattern to every transformer
block. Keeping an expensive attention core in one late Kimi layer therefore
requires retaining that core everywhere or changing model code. A block-qualified
save mapping lets a recipe spend a limited activation budget without changing
global expert recomputation or pipeline partitioning.

**Example.**

```python
from torchtitan.distributed.activation_remat import ActivationRematConfig

policy = ActivationRematConfig(
    save_regions=[],
    block_save_regions={"layers.91": ["attention.inner_attention"]},
)
# Only original layer 91 gains this save, including after a PP split.
# Explicit recompute_regions still take precedence.
```

## What changed

- Resolve original block-FQN globs into additive save-region patterns once when
  configuring existing checkpoints.
- Preserve global recompute precedence and saved-tensor-hook ownership; reject
  block overrides on fixed Full/default policies.
- Extend the component's REMAT.md and add numerical/ownership regressions next
  to activation-remat code.

The two forwarding-only recipe wrappers and their wrapper-only tests are
removed. The full-scale consumer constructs this existing policy field directly.

## Alternatives considered

- A global attention save retains the core in every layer and spends more memory.
- Model-specific checkpoint branches duplicate the existing region mechanism.
- Another checkpoint engine or backend arena setting is unnecessary; this only
  selects regions declared by the model.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Save patterns apply uniformly to every block. | Optional block-FQN globs add saves only to matching original blocks. |
| Full/default presets have fixed policies. | They still reject customization; use ActivationRematConfig explicitly. |

The default mapping is empty. Extra retained tensors follow existing pack/unpack
hooks and do not resize Dist-MoE's own activation arena.

## Numerics and testing

Fresh retained-parent checks: **138 CPU tests** and **four GPU-0-only graph
probes** pass.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' python -m pytest -q -o addopts= --tb=short \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/distributed/test_activation_remat.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/models/common/test_dist_moe.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/test_trainer.py \
  tests/unit_tests/cpu/recipes/test_shared_expert_overlap.py
```

CPU regressions verify exact loss, input/parameter gradients, original PP layer
IDs, additive glob/global saves, recompute precedence, fixed-preset rejection,
and saved-tensor-hook ownership. GPU probes cover FP32/BF16 with and without an
explicit recompute override: five changing-input captured-graph updates match
the uncheckpointed reference exactly in loss, input/parameter gradients, and
every parameter update. Assertions and deterministic execution remain strict.

All non-type hooks pass. Historical two-GPU PP2/VPP2 checks are separate
evidence, not fresh results from this one-GPU review.

## Landing gates

Fresh full-Kimi retention memory/performance, multi-rank PP/CP/FSDP, and
checkpoint resume remain unverified. Final-tip type checking, complete CI,
and maintainer review are still needed.

@@ -0,0 +1,183 @@
+# Copyright (c) Meta Platforms, Inc. and affiliates.
+# All rights reserved.
+#
+# This source code is licensed under the BSD-style license found in the
+# LICENSE file in the root directory of this source tree.
+
+"""Block-scoped activation retention preserves the global checkpoint policy."""
+
+from copy import deepcopy
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch_remat as remat
+
+from torchtitan.distributed.activation_remat import (
+    ActivationRematConfig,
+    DefaultActivationRematConfig,
+    FullActivationRematConfig,
+)
+from torchtitan.models.base.module import Module, ModuleDict
+from torchtitan.models.common.linear import Linear
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def deterministic_numerics():
+    """Exercise real finite computations with reproducible CPU inputs."""
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    previous = torch.are_deterministic_algorithms_enabled()
+    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(previous)
+
+
+class _Block(Module):
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.inner_compute = Linear.Config(in_features=32, out_features=32).build()
+        self.inner_forwards = 0
+        self.activation_forwards = 0
+
+    def _inner(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        self.inner_forwards += 1
+        return torch.nn.functional.linear(x_TD, self.inner_compute.weight)
+
+    def _activation(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        self.activation_forwards += 1
+        return x_TD.tanh()
+
+    def forward(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        output_TD = remat.region(
+            self._inner,
+            self.remat_region_name("inner_attention"),
+            recompute=self.remat_should_recompute("inner_attention"),
+        )(x_TD)
+        output_TD = remat.region(
+            self._activation,
+            self.remat_region_name("activation"),
+            recompute=self.remat_should_recompute("activation"),
+        )(output_TD)
+        remat.recompute_needs_tensor(output_TD)
+        return output_TD.sin()
+
+
+class _Model(Module):
+    def __init__(self, layer_ids: tuple[str, ...] = ("0", "1", "2")):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.layers = ModuleDict({layer_id: _Block() for layer_id in layer_ids})
+
+    def forward(self, x_TD: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        for block in self.layers.values():
+            x_TD = block(x_TD)
+        return x_TD
+
+
+def _run(model: _Model, input_TD: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+    """Return exact loss, input gradient, and parameter gradients."""
+    model.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
+    x_TD = input_TD.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+    loss = model(x_TD).square().sum()
+    loss.backward()
+    return (
+        loss.detach(),
+        x_TD.grad.detach().clone(),
+        *(parameter.grad.detach().clone() for parameter in model.parameters()),
+    )
+
+
+def test_only_selected_block_avoids_recomputation() -> None:
+    """One retained region skips replay only in its selected layer, exactly."""
+    reference = _Model()
+    actual = deepcopy(reference)
+    ActivationRematConfig(
+        save_regions=[], block_save_regions={"layers.1": ["inner_attention"]}
+    ).apply(actual)
+    input_TD = torch.randn(8, 32)
+    for actual_tensor, expected in zip(
+        _run(actual, input_TD), _run(reference, input_TD), strict=True
+    ):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_tensor, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert [block.inner_forwards for block in actual.layers.values()] == [2, 1, 2]
+
+
+def test_block_globs_preserve_pipeline_layer_fqns() -> None:
+    """A PP subset retains original IDs rather than renumbering its local layers."""
+    model = _Model(("81", "82", "91"))
+    ActivationRematConfig(
+        save_regions=[], block_save_regions={"layers.8?": ["inner_attention"]}
+    ).apply(model)
+    _run(model, torch.randn(8, 32))
+    assert [block.inner_forwards for block in model.layers.values()] == [1, 1, 2]
+
+
+def test_global_recompute_overrides_block_retention() -> None:
+    """An explicit recompute pattern still wins over additional block saves."""
+    model = _Model()
+    ActivationRematConfig(
+        save_regions=[],
+        recompute_regions=["inner_attention"],
+        block_save_regions={"layers.*": ["inner_attention"]},
+    ).apply(model)
+    _run(model, torch.randn(8, 32))
+    assert [block.inner_forwards for block in model.layers.values()] == [2, 2, 2]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "policy", [FullActivationRematConfig, DefaultActivationRematConfig]
+)
+def test_fixed_checkpoint_presets_reject_block_overrides(policy) -> None:
+    """Fixed Full and default remat presets cannot silently acquire custom saves."""
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ActivationRematConfig"):
+        policy(block_save_regions={"layers.1": ["inner_attention"]})
+
+
+def test_block_rules_are_additive_with_global_saves() -> None:
+    """Overlapping block globs never replace global or earlier matching saves."""
+    reference = _Model()
+    actual = deepcopy(reference)
+    ActivationRematConfig(
+        save_regions=["activation"],
+        block_save_regions={
+            "layers.*": ["inner_attention"],
+            "layers.1": [],
+        },
+    ).apply(actual)
+    input_TD = torch.randn(8, 32)
+    for actual_tensor, expected in zip(
+        _run(actual, input_TD), _run(reference, input_TD), strict=True
+    ):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_tensor, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert [block.inner_forwards for block in actual.layers.values()] == [1, 1, 1]
+    assert [block.activation_forwards for block in actual.layers.values()] == [1, 1, 1]
+
+
+def test_block_retention_respects_saved_tensor_hooks() -> None:
+    """Selected region outputs use the existing saved-tensor hook ownership."""
+    reference = _Model()
+    actual = deepcopy(reference)
+    saved_outputs = {}
+
+    def hooks(module, block_fqn):
+        def pack(tensor):
+            if (
+                remat.current_saved_tensor_info().kind
+                is remat.SavedTensorKind.SAVE_OUTPUT
+            ):
+                saved_outputs[block_fqn] = (
+                    saved_outputs.get(block_fqn, 0) + tensor.numel()
+                )
+            return tensor.detach().clone()
+
+        return pack, lambda payload: payload
+
+    ActivationRematConfig(
+        save_regions=[], block_save_regions={"layers.1": ["inner_attention"]}
+    ).apply(actual, saved_tensors_hooks=hooks)
+    input_TD = torch.randn(8, 32)
+    for actual_tensor, expected in zip(
+        _run(actual, input_TD), _run(reference, input_TD), strict=True
+    ):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_tensor, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    assert saved_outputs == {"layers.1": 8 * 32}
